text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Presidents Elias Hrawi and Hafez al-Assad hold summit meeting in Damascus today.
-U.S. Secretary of State told Prime Minister Hariri in Washington that lifting the ban on the travel of Americans to Lebanon depends on the security situation there.
-Minister of Social Affairs Estefan ad-Douwaihi says 30 percent of the Lebanese people live under the poverty line.
-The five-nation Lebanon ceasefire agreement monitoring committee transfers the Lebanese complaint against Israel to the concerned countries' foreign ministers.
-About 20 Lebanese held for hours at an Israeli checkpoint in south Lebanon.
-Hrawi postpones his consultations with MPs to nominate a prime minister until French President Jacques Chirac ends his visit to Lebanon on October 25.
-Syrian Information Minister Salman says the Syrian army has taken measures to confront any possible Israeli attack against the Golan Heights and Lebanon.
-Hariri to hold talks with U.S. President Clinton at the White House today.
